case_studies.title: Towards an Agent Operating System - Lessons from Classical and Cloud OS
case_studies.abstract: Every major wave of platform software follows the same arc: an initial period of experimentation with competing frameworks and ad-hoc implementations, followed by the articulation of a small set of stable abstractions with well-defined semantics, and finally consolidation around those abstractions into a platform that applications can portably target. POSIX did this for classical operating systems; Kubernetes did it for the cloud. Agentic AI systems - autonomous, LLM-driven agents that plan, use tools, maintain memory, and collaborate - are currently in the experimentation phase of the third s
case_studies.summary: This research aims to create an operating system for autonomous AI agents, building on lessons from classical and cloud operating systems. The authors analyzed the development of platforms like POSIX and Kubernetes to inform their work on an agent operating system. The result is a framework for understanding how to create a stable platform for AI agents.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that supports AI workloads, here is what to do: monitor the development of agent operating systems, assess their potential impact on your infrastructure, and consider how they might change your deployment strategies. This flags a risk: if your org uses cloud-based AI tools, check your platform's compatibility with emerging agent operating systems immediately. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant for those supporting AI and machine learning applications.
case_studies.relevance_tag: IT-relevant paper with potential for future applicability
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper discusses agentic AI systems, which is a novel concept for IT engineers. The mention of Kubernetes and POSIX operating systems suggests some relevance to IT systems. The paper provides some lessons from classical and cloud OS, which could be applicable to the design of future AI systems, but this is more of a long-term potential.

case_studies.title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM
case_studies.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models commonly adopt an LLM-centric $V \to L \to A$ pathway, where visual observations are projected into the representation space of a large language model before being decoded into robot actions. Although effective, this design incurs substantial computation and memory overhead at every policy invocation. In this work, we introduce TurboVLA, a new VLA paradigm that reformulates the conventional $V \to L \to A$ pathway as a direct $V + L \to A$ mapping. Instead of using a large language model as the central interface between perception and action, TurboVLA indepe
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of high computation and memory overhead in vision-language-action models by introducing TurboVLA, a new paradigm that maps visual and language inputs directly to actions. The researchers built TurboVLA, which can run at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with less than 1 GB VRAM. The result is a more efficient and faster model for real-time applications.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on AI model optimization for specific hardware rather than general cloud infrastructure management. If your organization develops or uses vision-language-action models, this research may be of interest for potential optimization opportunities. No immediate action is required for general IT infrastructure management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper reveals novel approach to VLA models. While not an IT paper in the classical sense, it does discuss LLM APIs. However, its value to real-world deployment within 90 days is limited by its focus on a specific, albeit new, AI design paradigm.

case_studies.title: Improving Item Discoverability in e-Commerce Search via Related Intent Generation
case_studies.abstract: Traditional search systems are optimized to retrieve items that strictly match a query, often prioritizing precision over recall. In e-commerce marketplaces and particularly grocery, this paradigm is limiting, as user satisfaction and commercial outcomes depend heavily on the discoverability of substitute, complementary, and thematically related items. In this paper, we present a scalable system for discovery-augmented search that leverages intent-conditioned recall expansion. Our approach generates implicit user intents to expand candidate recall while maintaining relevance. The system addres
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited item discoverability in e-commerce search by building a system that generates related intents to expand search results, resulting in improved recall without sacrificing relevance. The system uses intent-conditioned recall expansion to suggest substitute, complementary, and thematically related items. This is not directly relevant to cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on improving e-commerce search functionality rather than cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty is moderate, but not directly relevant to IT infrastructure or deployment. Real-world impact and practical maturity are moderate, but it's focused on search systems rather than IT-specific applications.

case_studies.title: Failures Reveal What Metrics Miss: An Evidence-Driven Agent for Recursive Refinement of ECG Classifiers
case_studies.abstract: Deep models have substantially advanced 12-lead ECG classification, yet their refinement still relies heavily on human experts to inspect failures and iteratively revise classifier designs. Recent LLM-based agents have demonstrated the potential for automated model design, but when guided only by aggregate performance metrics, they lack insight into why individual cases fail and how the classifier should be revised. We present RecursiveECG, an evidence-driven LLM-as-Designer framework in which an LLM serves as an offline model designer that refines ECG classifiers based on concrete failures an
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of refining ECG classifiers by using a framework that automatically identifies and learns from failures, building a more accurate classifier. The authors built RecursiveECG, a framework that uses a large language model to refine ECG classifiers. The result is a more accurate ECG classifier that can learn from its mistakes.
case_studies.it_breakdown: This is not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on refining ECG classification models in a medical context.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Interesting approach to refining ECG classifiers with LLMs, but relevance to IT infrastructure is low. Could be a starting point for a consultant exploring agentic systems or MLOps.

case_studies.title: Living-Harness Is an Interactive-Agent Evolver
case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents may recover from a failure within an episode or after a retry, yet the same execution failure can recur in later tasks because post-episode feedback rarely revises the persistent harness that guides future interactions. Static harnesses improve reliability through fixed tools, context, memory, and workflow structures, but remain unchanged after deployment. We propose $\textbf{Living-Harness}$, a self-evolving agent harness that converts each completed trajectory and its evaluator signals into posterior evidence for bounded harness updates. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of large language model agents failing due to static harnesses that don't adapt to new information. The researchers built a self-evolving agent harness called Living-Harness that updates itself based on completed tasks and feedback. The result is improved reliability and reduced execution failures.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on improving large language model agents rather than cloud infrastructure management. If you're involved in AI or machine learning projects, this might be of interest, but it doesn't require immediate action from IT infrastructure managers. No specific steps are needed to apply this research to cloud infrastructure work.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper proposes a novel concept for self-evolving agent harnesses, but lacks context on current IT solutions for these issues. Novelty is somewhat mitigated by limited real-world application. Could potentially be used to improve DevOps automation or MLOps in 90 days with significant development.

case_studies.title: Model-Driven Requirements Configuration with Three-Valued Uncertainty Scoring
case_studies.abstract: Context: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer natural-language flexibility for automated requirements elicitation but frequently generate structurally invalid requirements and logical inconsistencies, lacking formal correctness guarantees. Objectives: This study aims to eliminate logical inconsistencies and enforce structural conformance in LLM-generated requirements while quantifying the LLM's pre-validation decision uncertainty within a formal domain model. Methods: We present a neuro-symbolic multi-agent architecture that operationalizes the Object-Oriented Method for Requirements Authoring a
case_studies.summary: This research aims to improve the accuracy of automated requirements elicitation using Large Language Models by eliminating logical inconsistencies and enforcing structural conformance. The researchers built a neuro-symbolic multi-agent architecture to achieve this. The result is a more reliable way to generate requirements, but it's not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on improving requirements elicitation for software development. If your organization uses automated requirements elicitation tools, you may want to monitor future developments in this area. However, no immediate action is required for cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: High IT relevance due to LLM deployment angle. Moderate novelty due to uncertainty scoring in LLM-generated requirements. Limited value within 90 days due to complex architecture and potential high implementation costs.
